summary: The candidate changes the DeepSeek-V4 metric from zero to the exact tensor-byte total for the exercised standard FP8, HIP FP4-indexer, and unified-KV layouts. It does not fully satisfy the original contract for HiSparse: HiSparseC4DevicePool owns an additional GPU data_ptrs tensor, but DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool.allocated_tensors() returns only kv_buffer, so top-level mem_usage under-reports that active layout. The submitted tests and GPU verifier omit this tensor and therefore do not detect the counterexample.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual gfx950 allocations reproduced inherited mem_usage=0 for non-unified FP8, HIP FP4 indexer, HiSparse, and unified layouts despite independently counted owned tensors of 3,594,944; 3,588,800; 3,594,952; and 4,099,456 bytes respectively.
Candidate's focused regression file passed: 5 tests and 8 subtests.

Actual gfx950 allocations matched exactly for standard FP8 (3,594,944 bytes), HIP FP4 indexer (3,588,800 bytes), and unified KV (4,099,456 bytes), but HiSparse reported 3,594,944 bytes versus 3,594,952 bytes physically owned.
Candidate patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) executed real torch allocations for standard FP8, HIP FP4-indexer, HiSparse, and unified-KV layouts; see evidence/base_actual_pool.txt and evidence/candidate_actual_pool.txt.
remaining_counterexamples: With enable_hisparse=True, HiSparseC4DevicePool allocates self.data_ptrs on the GPU, but the candidate's allocated_tensors() inherited from DeepSeekV4SingleKVPool returns only self.kv_buffer. The reduced one-C4-layer run reports 3,594,944 bytes while the pool owns 3,594,952 bytes.
remaining_limitations: DeepSeek-V4/DeepSeek-V4-Flash weights were unavailable, so no full server launch or HTTP metrics scrape was performed.

The original 8-rank NVIDIA H100 environment was unavailable. Validation used one assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), so it does not qualify CUDA, multi-GPU, tensor-parallel, pipeline-parallel, or model-semantic behavior.
NPU hardware and torch_npu were unavailable. NPU accounting was source-reviewed but not executed.
No native source changed in the candidate; a native rebuild was not applicable. Python imported sglang from /job/repo/python/sglang and torch from /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch.
